newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian budget can repair savings - Fraser.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian budget can repair savings - Fraser.

text.p: Outgoing Australian Reserve Bank governor Bernie Fraser said the government's budget strategy could reverse the country's historic decline in national savings.

"If it is realised, this budget strategy, in combination with the planned increases in compulsory retirement provisions, will go a long way towards reversing the deterioration in national saving which has been on-going since the 1970s," he told a business seminar.
The government had forecast a budget deficit falling to about one percent of GDP in the fiscal year to June 1997 from about two percent in 1995/96, the governor said.
The budget would be close to balance in two years, he added.

"In addition, the present government has committed itself to a fiscal strategy which seeks to balance out budget deficits and surpluses over the course of the business cycle -- and thereby avoid any net increase in government debt over the course of the cycle."
The Liberal-National government's fiscal tightening, worth A$7.2 billion in 1997/98, depends on the necessary laws passing the upper house of parliament, the Senate.
While the Labor opposition says the overall shape of the budget will survive, it could lose measures worth hundreds of millions of Australian dollars per year.
